title: cookie-consent-validator: a command line test for whether cookie banners honour rejection
description:
Node.js command line tool that drives a real browser, clicks "Reject All" on a site's consent banner, waits for the banner to be dismissed, then measures what survived: tracking cookies still set, tracker requests still firing, and web-storage keys matching known tracker patterns. Built to measure the gap between a banner that looks compliant and one that behaves as it claims. Recognises the common consent management platforms and exits non-zero when violations are found.

Documentation: https://trustyourwebsite.github.io/cookie-consent-validator/. Released on npm as @trustyourwebsite/cookie-consent-validator under the MIT licence.

Maintained by TrustYourWebsite, which runs this check and others as a hosted scanner for businesses in the EU and the UK, and by Get Up to Code, the same scanner for the United States and Canada. This tool performs technical analysis and does not provide legal advice.
